document_check.note: Document is Agbavor and Liang (2024) 'Multilingual Prediction of Cognitive Impairment with Large Language Models and Speech Analysis', Brain Sciences 14:1292, an INTERSPEECH 2024 TAUKADIAL Challenge entry. Table 6 (p8) gives test-set balanced accuracy 0.612 (language-agnostic) vs 0.818 (language-specific), and Table 5 gives the English-to-Chinese transfer results.

cited_result: Unseen TAUKADIAL test set (40 participants): balanced accuracy (UAR) 0.612 for the language-agnostic Whisper-embedding neural network vs 0.818 for the language-specific ensemble; secondary: English-trained models inferring on Chinese picture-description tasks had balanced accuracy 0.418 to 0.529.
tool_reason: The cited result compares the classification performance of machine-learning MCI-versus-normal classifiers (language-agnostic vs language-specific), so PROBAST with the PROBAST+AI considerations applies.

domains.rationale: The data are a challenge set of MCI patients and normal controls matched on age and sex by propensity scores, which is a case-control style sample rather than a consecutive clinical cohort; recruitment, eligibility and exclusions are not described.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used (e.g. cohort, RCT or nested case-control data)?
signalling.quote: The dataset is curated to ensure a balanced representation of age and sex among participants, thereby mitigating potential confounding factors and bias using a propensity score matching approach [25,26].

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched for eligibility, inclusion or exclusion criteria and recruitment: the only description is 'collected while the speakers participated in picture description tasks conducted as cognitive assessments in clinical settings.'

domains.rationale: Predictors are automated Whisper acoustic embeddings extracted the same way for all recordings within a language, blind to diagnosis, and available at the time of intended use. The picture stimuli differ between languages, which matters for the cross-language comparison rather than for bias in the within-language test result.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: It is important to note that the pictures used for descriptions in each language were different.

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: In this study, we utilize the whisper-large-v3 model for acoustic feature extraction.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: It allows for easy and non-invasive sample collection, streamlining the assessment process.

domains.rationale: How MCI and normal cognition were diagnosed, by whom, with what criteria, and whether the picture-description task informed diagnosis are not reported (deferred to the challenge paper).

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for MCI diagnostic criteria or procedure: only 'speakers of Mandarin Chinese and English with different levels of cognitive impairment as well as individuals with normal cognition (NC) [25].'

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: Searched for 'criteria', 'Petersen', 'diagnos': no definition of MCI given.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: collected while the speakers participated in picture description tasks conducted as cognitive assessments in clinical settings.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Searched for whether English and Chinese sites used the same diagnostic procedure: not reported.

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of diagnosticians to speech recordings: not reported.

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: collected while the speakers participated in picture description tasks conducted as cognitive assessments in clinical settings.

domains.rationale: Very small samples (129 training and 40 test participants) for 1280-dimensional embeddings; three recordings per person with leave-one-task-out validation that places the same participants on both sides (Tables 2, 3, 5); a validation split with no statement that it is at participant level; test predictions manually checked before submission; no calibration or confidence intervals; normalisation fold-wise status unreported; feature family chosen by performance; and the compared pipelines differ in more than language-specificity (single NN vs three-model majority-vote ensemble).

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: The training dataset comprises 387 voice recordings from 129 participants from MCI patients and normal cognition (NC) subjects. The test dataset consists of 120 recordings from 40 participants.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: These embeddings were further normalized by using z-score normalization

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for excluded participants or recordings: none reported.

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for 'missing' and data exclusions: none reported.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: Comparisons of linguistic features with other multilingual embedding models did not yield improved performance. Therefore, the results reported in this work are based only on acoustic features.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: This involved training three different machine learning models, each using two of the three picture-description tasks for training and the third task for testing.

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately (including calibration)?
signalling.quote: For the MCI classification task, we assess model performance using the following metrics from the challenge: unweighted average recall (UAR, also called balanced accuracy), specificity, sensitivity, and F1 Score.

signalling.question: 4.8 Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism in model performance accounted for?
signalling.quote: Finally, we manually checked the predictions to ensure consistency across the tasks for each subject before submission to the competition organizer.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI: Was the train/test split at participant level?
signalling.answer: Probably yes for the test set; No for the validation results
signalling.quote: The test dataset consists of 120 recordings from 40 participants.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI: Were preprocessing and tuning done within training folds only?
signalling.quote: Searched for whether z-score normalisation and hyperparameter search were fitted on training data only, and whether the 80/20 split was by participant: stated only as 'we use a stratified approach based on both the detected language and diagnosis when dividing the data'.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI: Was the test set held out from all tuning?
signalling.quote: To determine optimal hyperparameters for our models, we adopt a methodology that involves dividing the training data into an 80/20 split for training and validation sets.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI: Was class imbalance handled?
signalling.quote: Within the training set, 222 samples belong to the MCI group, while the remaining 165 samples are healthy control.

signalling.question: PROBAST+AI: Is the reported performance apparent, internally validated or externally validated?
signalling.answer: Internally validated (split-sample challenge test set from the same dataset)
signalling.quote: In Table 6, we show the results of the MCI classification task on the unseen test set.

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for final model specification: embedding-based classifiers, no weights reported.

applicability.rationale: Age- and sex-matched MCI and controls from a challenge set, Mandarin and English speakers, with no stated diagnostic criteria; not a clinical MCI population.
Speech recordings from picture description are feasible in practice.

overall_rationale: Domain 1 is high (propensity-matched case-control style challenge sample) and domain 4 is high (tiny samples for high-dimensional inputs, clustered recordings, manual checking of test predictions, no calibration or intervals, non-like-for-like pipelines); domain 3 is unclear because the MCI diagnosis is undescribed.
